metadata.title: AI Foundations Control Theory — Sources
metadata.description: Primary references for 12 control-theory primitives: PID, feedback/feedforward, observability, controllability, Lyapunov stability, MPC, Kalman filter, dead-time compensation, anti-windup, gain scheduling, circuit breaker, backpressure, rate limiting, and DeePC/behavioral systems

textbooks.name: Feedback Systems: An Introduction for Scientists and Engineers
textbooks.description: Åström & Murray (2020). Canonical graduate-level textbook on feedback control. Covers PID, state-space, Lyapunov, MPC, Kalman filter, and dead-time compensation. Free PDF available at fbsbook.org. Primary source for primitives #1–#9.

textbooks.name: Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems
textbooks.description: Franklin, Powell & Emami-Naeini, 8th ed. (2019). Standard undergraduate/graduate control textbook. Covers PID tuning, state-space, Kalman filter, MPC, and root locus. Primary source for primitives #1, #2, #3, #6, #7, #8.

textbooks.name: Modern Control Engineering
textbooks.description: Ogata, K., 5th ed. (2010). Comprehensive control engineering reference. Source for observability, controllability, and Lyapunov stability (primitives #3, #4).

textbooks.name: Feedback Control of Computing Systems
textbooks.description: Hellerstein, Diao, Parekh & Tilbury (2004). Wiley. The definitive reference applying control theory to computing systems — web servers, databases, operating systems. Source for computing-domain applications across all 11 primitives.

textbooks.name: Model Predictive Control
textbooks.description: Camacho & Bordons, 2nd ed. (2007). Springer. Primary reference for MPC theory, receding horizon, constraint handling, and stability (primitive #5).

textbooks.name: Release It! Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software
textbooks.description: Nygard, M., 2nd ed. (2018). Pragmatic Bookshelf. Canonical practitioner reference for circuit breaker and stability patterns in distributed systems (primitive #10).

papers.name: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
papers.description: Kalman, R.E. (1960). ASME J. Basic Engineering 82:35-45. Original paper introducing the Kalman filter. Foundational source for primitive #6.

papers.name: Optimum Settings for Automatic Controllers
papers.description: Ziegler & Nichols (1942). ASME Trans. 64:759-768. Original paper introducing the Ziegler-Nichols PID tuning method. Source for primitive #1 tuning.

papers.name: Closer control of loops with dead time
papers.description: Smith, O.J.M. (1957). Chemical Engineering Progress 53(5):217-219. Original Smith Predictor paper for dead-time compensation. Source for primitive #7.

papers.name: Research on gain scheduling
papers.description: Rugh & Shamma (2000). Automatica 36(10):1401-1425. Survey of gain scheduling theory and practice. Source for primitive #9.

papers.name: The General Problem of the Stability of Motion
papers.description: Lyapunov, A.M. (1892, English translation 1992). Taylor & Francis. Original Lyapunov stability theory. Source for primitive #4.

papers.name: An Introduction to the Kalman Filter
papers.description: Welch & Bishop (2006). UNC-Chapel Hill TR 95-041. Accessible Kalman filter tutorial with discrete-time formulation. Secondary source for primitive #6.

papers.name: CircuitBreaker pattern
papers.description: Fowler, M. martinfowler.com. Practitioner description of the circuit breaker pattern with state machine. Secondary source for primitive #10.

papers.name: Network Algorithmics
papers.description: Varghese, G. (2004). Morgan Kaufmann. Token bucket and leaky bucket algorithms. Source for primitive #11.

papers.name: CBF-RL: Safety Filtering Reinforcement Learning in Training with Control Barrier Functions
papers.description: Yang, Werner, de Sa & Ames (2025/2026). ICRA 2026. Integrates control barrier functions into RL training rollouts, producing policies that are provably safe and operate without runtime safety filters. Hardware-validated on Unitree G1 humanoid. Code: https://github.com/lzyang2000/cbf-rl-navigation-demo. Extends primitive #4 (Lyapunov stability) to learned controllers.

papers.name: Stability of data-driven Koopman MPC with terminal conditions
papers.description: Schimperna, Bold, Köhler, Worthmann & Magni (2025/2026). arXiv:2511.21248. Proves recursive feasibility and asymptotic stability for MPC using kernel EDMD (Koopman operator) as data-driven surrogate, with terminal conditions and proportional error bound. Extends primitive #5 to nonlinear plants without an explicit model.

papers.name: Online Convex Optimization and Integral Quadratic Constraints: An automated approach to regret analysis
papers.description: Jakob & Iannelli (2025). IEEE CDC 2025. Applies Integral Quadratic Constraints (IQC) to derive automated regret guarantees for first-order OCO algorithms expressed as linear dynamical systems in feedback with monotone operators. Bridges classical control robustness analysis and online optimization. Relevant when combining adaptive/online MPC with formal guarantees.

papers.name: WVA: A Global Optimization Control Plane for llmd
papers.description: Malvankar et al. (2026). arXiv:2603.09730. Application-aware feedback autoscaler for LLM inference (Kubernetes/llm-d) that uses KV-cache saturation and queue depth as controlled variables. Achieves 37% throughput improvement and 10x failure reduction vs HPA. Open-source: https://github.com/llm-d-incubation/workload-variant-autoscaler. Instantiates primitives #5, #10, #11 for LLM serving.

papers.name: Data-Enabled Predictive Control: In the Shallows of the DeePC
papers.description: Coulson, Lygeros & Dörfler (2019). ECC 2019. Foundational DeePC paper. Replaces the explicit plant model in MPC with a Hankel matrix of past input-output trajectories, using Willems' Fundamental Lemma (2005). For LTI noiseless systems DeePC is equivalent to classical MPC. Verified via arXiv search 2026-05-17. Canonical source for primitive #12. Note: arXiv ID 1811.10455 is an unrelated ML paper — use 1811.05890.

papers.name: A note on persistency of excitation
papers.description: Willems, Rapisarda, Markovsky & De Moor (2005). Systems & Control Letters 54(4):325-329. Establishes that all trajectories of a controllable LTI system can be parameterized by the columns of a Hankel matrix built from a single persistently-exciting experiment. Theoretical backbone of DeePC and behavioral systems control. DOI is well-established in literature; treat as confirmed.

papers.name: Control-Oriented System Identification: Classical, Learning, and Physics-Informed Approaches
papers.description: Sivaranjani, Shi, Atanasov, Duong, Feng, Martin, Xu, Gupta & Allgöwer (2025). arXiv:2512.06315. Submitted 2025-12-06. Survey of control-oriented sysid covering classical, ML, and physics-informed approaches. Key finding: ML models trained without control-relevant constraints (dissipativity, stability) can destabilize control loops. Evidence grade B — arXiv only, no confirmed peer-review venue as of 2026-05-17.

papers.name: DeePC vs. Koopman MPC for Pasteurization: A Comparative Study
papers.description: Daráš, Valábek & Klaučo (2026). arXiv:2604.00524. Head-to-head comparison of DeePC and Koopman MPC on a multivariable pasteurization process. Finding: Koopman MPC tracks more tightly under the chosen cost; DeePC produces substantially smoother input trajectories. Verified via WebFetch 2026-07-11. Paper-only; single-process case study, generalizability to other plants unverified. Source for the DeePC-vs-Koopman tradeoff in primitive #12.

papers.name: Scalable Nonlinear DeePC: Bridging Direct and Indirect Methods and Basis Reduction
papers.description: de Jong, Lazar, Weiland & Dörfler (2025). arXiv:2512.14535. Studies regularized nonlinear DeePC; introduces SVD-based dimensionality reduction preserving equivalence with subspace predictive control (SPC). Verified via WebFetch 2026-07-11. arXiv preprint only; no confirmed peer-review venue as of 2026-07-11 — evidence grade B. Source for the Hankel-matrix-scaling fix in primitive #12.

papers.name: Predictive Autoscaling for Node.js on Kubernetes: Lower Latency, Right-Sized Capacity
papers.description: Tymoshenko, Maraschi & Collina (2026). arXiv:2604.19705. Feedforward-dominant predictive autoscaler for Node.js/Kubernetes. Confirmed empirical: 26ms median latency vs. 154ms for KEDA and 522ms for HPA under steady ramp load. Matteo Collina is Node.js core maintainer. Paper-only; no open code confirmed. Caveat: Node.js-specific; generalizability to other runtimes unverified. Source for Predictive Autoscaler composition recipe.

papers.name: Stable Agentic Control: Tool-Mediated LLM Architecture for Autonomous Cyber Defense
papers.description: Prinos, Brush, Denton, Wang, Knox, Antani, Foltz & Villaseñor (2026). arXiv:2605.03034. Applies Input-to-State Stability (ISS) formally to an LLM-based agentic system; Lyapunov function machine-checked in Lean 4. Key finding: finite action catalogs at tool interfaces guarantee stability independent of model capability or temperature. A tool-mediated Claude Sonnet 4 controller reduced attacker payoff by 59% vs. a deterministic greedy baseline; a Claude Haiku 4.5 controller stayed catalog-bounded despite converging to a suboptimal value. Confirms that stability must be baked into loop architecture, not delegated to the model. Extends primitive #4 (Lyapunov stability) to LLM agent loops. Paper-only; domain is autonomous cyber defense. Verified via WebFetch against arxiv.org/abs/2605.03034 on 2026-07-11 — full author list confirmed, no author named Iyer; earlier version of this record misattributed the paper.

papers.name: Probabilistic Control Barrier Functions for Systems with State Estimation Uncertainty using Sub-Gaussian Concentration
papers.description: Echigo, van Wijk, Mestres, Daş, Burdick & Ames (2026). arXiv:2604.08831. Particle-based probabilistic CBF framework providing tight probabilistic safety guarantees via sub-Gaussian concentration bounds and finite-sample CVaR estimates. Extends classical (deterministic) CBF to systems with sensor noise. Relevant when deterministic CBF is applied with noisy measurements. Paper-only; no code confirmed.
